newsitem.title: CHINA: HK works to avoid new airport cargo facility delay.
newsitem.headline: HK works to avoid new airport cargo facility delay.

text.p: Hong Kong's Airport Authority said on Friday it was doing all it could to ensure that the cargo handling facilities at the territory's new airport would be ready in time for the opening next April.

"The cargo handling equipment and other facilities and building services have been moving along steadily, but it is a challenging construction programme," the authority's chief executive Henry Townsend told government radio.
"Obviously, this is the reason why we want, first, to help them all we can, and two, to try to make sure that they will be able to operate on the airport opening."

Hong Kong Air Cargo Terminals (HACTL) is investing US$1 billion in its Superterminal One at the new Chek Lap Kok airport and says it will be the world's largest and most advanced cargo handling facility.
The US$9 billion airport is expected to handle 87 million passengers and nine million tonnes of cargo per year once the second of its two runways opens later in 1998.
Townsend said questions of a delayed opening for the cargo facility would have to wait until the Airport Authority holds meetings with the government in two months.
"I think any speculation beyond that is probably unwarranted, but that will be taken into consideration when we meet with the government in September," he said.

Last month, HACTL managing director Anthony Charter told Reuters he was seeking an overlap between the opening of Chek Lap Kok and the closing of the territory's existing Kai Tak airport to prevent potential chaos due to teething troubles.
Charter said the cargo handling facility at the new airport would only be 50 percent operational by next April and was not expected to be completely up to speed until two months later.
There is also concern the railway link to the new airport will not be ready on time.
In April, the Mass Transit Railway Corporation said it was looking at ways of advancing the opening of its airport railway to coincide with Chek Lap Kok's planned opening date.
The 34-km (20-mile), HK$35.1 billion railway will provide service between Hong Kong island and the new airport via the Kowloon peninsula, Tsing Yi Island and Lantau island.
